title: Ledger layout breaks between 900px and 1100px
description:
The three-column grid on the home page uses a fixed 186px rail and a fixed 190px tag column. Below roughly 1100px viewport width the title column is squeezed to nothing and every row in the works index wraps.

Measured title-column width (centre column minus year, gaps and tag):
  901px  ->  49px   every row wraps
  1024px -> 148px   every row wraps, several double-height
  1100px -> 248px   tight
  1180px -> 328px   correct

The mobile breakpoint sits at 900px, so there is a ~200px band the design never handles. 1024px is iPad landscape and a common laptop window, so this is the single most visible defect on the site. Confirmed visually: 'Resonant Landscapes', 'A more perfect union' and 'And the water receded' all break to two lines.

Fix options: let the tag column size to content (max-content or minmax) instead of a fixed 190px, or raise the mobile breakpoint from 900px to ~1100px so the narrow layout covers the gap.
acceptance_criteria: No work row exceeds single-line height at any viewport width from 900px to 1400px. Verified by measuring row heights in the browser, not by eyeballing.
close_reason: Tag column now sizes to its own content (max-content) instead of a fixed 190px, which decouples the widest title from the widest tag — they never occur in the same row — and drops the worst row's requirement from 510px to 433px. A new breakpoint at 1140px drops the hover-driven preview panel below that and holds the ledger to an 860px measure, so rows keep their horizontal shape down to the 900px mobile stack. Measured in-browser: no title or tag wraps at 901, 1024, 1141, 1180, 1400. Note the acceptance criterion's 900px floor is read as 901+; at 900 and below the stacked layout is the intended design.

title: Work page bodies don't share a register or a minimum
description:
The writing half of tc-c8k, split out once the structural half landed. The
frontmatter question — what belongs in a field rather than in prose — is
settled and done. How the pages read is not.

LENGTH — 0 to 346 words, median 132:

  pseudo-pseudo     0    no prose at all, only a performance bullet
  si               23    a directing credit and nothing else
  swarm            35
  veins-of-the-earth 36
  ...
  sounds-aware    339
  immaterial-cloud 346

The shortest read as stubs beside the longest, which read as papers. Note the
migration's own comment on pseudo-pseudo already says the source post 'has no
prose whatsoever' and that its blurb is 'still worth replacing with a real one'.

VOICE — three, sometimes on the same page:

  - First person, and the most alive writing on the site: 'I thought it would be
    interesting to make a piece out of a daily task', 'Working on this piece was
    also a sort of therapy.'
  - Impersonal third person: 'The composition invites immersive, contemplative
    listening.'
  - Paper abstract, pasted verbatim. resonant-landscapes carries a whole
    '## Abstract' saying 'This paper details the technical implementation of the
    project' and 'We discuss how frugal innovation principles guided our design
    choices' — a paper describing itself, in the first person plural, on a page
    that is about the work rather than the paper. sounds-aware does the same.

SECTIONS — '## Performances' on 12 works, '## Exhibitions' on 4, both on
a-more-perfect-union, neither on 6. Nothing distinguishes when a showing counts
as one or the other.

TWO LEFT DELIBERATELY during the structural pass, because both are prose rather
than bare links and moving them mechanically would have broken the sentences
around them:

  - a-more-perfect-union: 'Try it: <https://sparkling-sun-445.fly.dev/>', which
    has a note under it referring back to 'the link'.
  - sounds-aware: a '[Dissertation]' link opening the 2021 section.

This is Tate's own writing, carried over from the archive, so the register is his
call rather than something to standardize unilaterally — the same constraint as
tc-2zm, and the same answer should cover both. The work blurbs are already the
strongest and most consistent writing on the site; they are the model to work
back from.
design:
src/content/works/*.md. The 21 archived bodies are generated by
scripts/migrate.mjs, so edits to the markdown alone are overwritten on a re-run
— a rewrite of any size needs either a BODY_FIXES entry per work or a decision
to stop treating those files as generated, which is probably the right call once
the prose stops being the archive's. drift.md is hand-authored and outside that.

BODY_FIXES now throws if a pattern matches nothing, so a stale entry fails the
migration rather than silently reverting a body.

One incidental defect to sweep up: swarm opens 'is an live-sampling instrument'.
acceptance_criteria:
A stated convention for what a work body contains — roughly how long, what it
opens with, whose voice — recorded where the next person will find it. Every
work page follows it. No paper abstract is pasted in as prose. pseudo-pseudo and
si either have a body or are a deliberate, recorded exception. Performances and
Exhibitions are used by a stated rule.
notes:
Split from tc-c8k on 2026-08-07. tc-c8k's structural half — url and repo moved
into frontmatter, duplicate link rows and paper links removed — shipped in PR #3
and closed. Related: tc-2zm is the same register question on about.md and should
be decided alongside this. tc-89d depends on this issue.

title: Work page bodies have no shared shape or register
description:
Across the 22 work pages the body copy varies in length, in what it opens
with, in who is speaking, and in what it assumes the reader already saw. Read
back to back they do not sound like one catalogue.

LENGTH — 0 to 346 words, median 132:

  pseudo-pseudo     0    no prose at all, only a performance bullet
  si               23    a directing credit and nothing else
  swarm            35
  veins-of-the-earth 36
  ...
  sounds-aware    339
  immaterial-cloud 346

The four shortest read as stubs next to the longest four, which read as papers.

OPENING — three different conventions:

  - Prose, the majority: 'This piece is a result of the restrictions of
    recording directly to tape.'
  - A bare link row: resonant-landscapes opens '[Installation] | [Paper] |
    [Code]', immaterial-cloud opens 'visit: [imamterial.cloud]'.
  - A bare credit line: si is 'Short film directed by Samantha Aldana, 2015'.

VOICE — at least three:

  - First person, and the most alive: 'I thought it would be interesting to make
    a piece out of a daily task', 'Working on this piece was also a sort of
    therapy.'
  - Impersonal third person: 'The composition invites immersive, contemplative
    listening.'
  - Paper abstract, pasted verbatim. resonant-landscapes carries a whole
    '## Abstract' that says 'This paper details the technical implementation of
    the project' and 'We discuss how frugal innovation principles guided our
    design choices' — a paper describing itself, in the first person plural, on
    a page that is about the work rather than about the paper. sounds-aware does
    the same.

DUPLICATION with what the template already renders. The page prints title,
blurb, medium, collaborators, the research box and a 'Project site' link above
the body, and several bodies restate that material:

  - resonant-landscapes' opening link row repeats the Audio Mostly paper that
    the research box already links two inches above it.
  - resonant-landscapes and immaterial-cloud both have live project sites
    expressed as ad-hoc markdown in the body. Only drift.md actually sets the
    'url' frontmatter field the template renders. That part is mechanical and
    worth doing regardless of the writing.
  - drift restates its materials three times — filed separately as tc-zis, but
    it is one instance of this same problem.

SECTIONS — '## Performances' on 12 works, '## Exhibitions' on 4, both on
a-more-perfect-union, neither on 6. Nothing distinguishes when a showing counts
as one or the other.

Most of this prose is Tate's own, carried over from the archive, so the register
the pages should settle on is his call rather than something to standardize
unilaterally — the same reason tc-2zm is still open. What can be decided first
is the shape: what a body opens with, roughly how long it runs, what belongs in
frontmatter instead of prose, and whether a paper abstract belongs on a work
page at all or should be a link to the paper.

Worth noting the blurbs are already the strongest writing on the site and are
consistent with each other. They are the model to work back from.
design:
src/content/works/*.md for the bodies. The mechanical half — moving project
URLs into the 'url' frontmatter field, dropping link rows that duplicate the
research box — touches only frontmatter and needs no writing decisions, and
could land first as its own change.

Bodies for the 21 archived works are generated by scripts/migrate.mjs, so edits
to the markdown alone are overwritten on a re-run. Substantial rewrites want
either a BODY_FIXES entry per work or a decision to stop treating those files as
generated. drift.md is hand-authored and outside that.

Two incidental defects to sweep up in the same pass: immaterial-cloud's link
text reads 'imamterial.cloud', and swarm opens 'is an live-sampling instrument'.
acceptance_criteria:
A written convention for what a work body contains, recorded somewhere the next
person will find it. Every work page follows it: none opens on a bare link row
or credit line, no body restates the blurb, medium or research box, no paper
abstract is pasted in as prose, and every live project site is in the 'url'
field. pseudo-pseudo and si either have a body or are a deliberate exception.
Performances and Exhibitions are used by a stated rule.
notes:
Raised after noticing the variability while reading the pages back to back.
Possibly wants splitting: the frontmatter and structural half is mechanical and
independently shippable, the rewriting half is a writing pass that only Tate can
do. Related: tc-2zm (bio register), tc-zis (drift's materials), tc-89d (two of
these bodies link to the old site's absolute URLs).
Cross-references made after review: tc-zis (drift's materials listed three
times) was a strict subset of this issue's 'no body restates the blurb, medium
or research box' criterion and has been superseded by it — drift still needs
that fix, it is just covered here now. tc-89d now depends on this one, so the
URL corrections land on bodies whose shape is already settled rather than being
redone after. tc-2zm is the same register question on about.md and should be
decided alongside this, though neither blocks the other.

--- 2026-08-07, structural half done (branch fix/frontmatter-urls-and-docs) ---

Landed, no writing decisions involved:

  - Added an optional 'repo' field to the schema. Three bodies carried a bare
    '[Code](github…)' link in three different places; the template now renders
    'Source ↗' beside 'Project site ↗' from frontmatter.
  - url:  resonant-landscapes, immaterial-cloud (drift already had one)
    repo: resonant-landscapes, mesh-garden, sounds-aware
  - Removed the link rows those replaced, including two '[Paper]' links that
    duplicated the research box rendered directly above the body, and drift's
    '[Project site]' line that duplicated its own frontmatter.
  - immaterial-cloud's 'imamterial.cloud' typo went with its line.
  - New URLS and REPOS maps in scripts/migrate.mjs so all of it survives a
    re-run. Every URL verified 200 on 2026-08-07.
  - BODY_FIXES now throws if a pattern matches nothing. Two entries had been
    given the same slug key while making this change, and the later silently
    replaced the earlier — which would have quietly reverted the tc-24p heading
    fix with no signal. Tested against a deliberately altered archive copy.

Still open, all of it writing:

  - Length still runs 0 to 346 words. pseudo-pseudo and si still have no body.
  - The pasted paper abstracts in resonant-landscapes and sounds-aware.
  - First person vs impersonal third person vs paper register.
  - a-more-perfect-union's 'Try it: <url>' is prose with a dependent note under
    it, so it was left rather than mechanically hoisted into the url field.
  - sounds-aware's '[Dissertation]' link, same reason.
  - Performances vs Exhibitions still has no stated rule.
  - swarm still opens 'is an live-sampling instrument'.
close_reason:
Split. The structural half is done and shipped in PR #3: an optional 'repo' field on the schema, project sites and repositories moved out of the prose into url/repo frontmatter for five works via new URLS and REPOS maps in scripts/migrate.mjs, the ad-hoc link rows removed along with two paper links that duplicated the research box and drift's duplicate of its own url, and immaterial-cloud's 'imamterial.cloud' typo gone with its line. BODY_FIXES now throws on a pattern that matches nothing.

The writing half — length, register, the pasted paper abstracts, the two empty bodies, the Performances/Exhibitions rule — is tc-af1. Closing rather than reopening because this issue's acceptance criteria were already half satisfied, which would have made it ambiguous to pick up later.

title: Add 404 page, robots.txt, sitemap, favicon and og:image
description:
Standard files the site does not have:

  - No 404.html. A mistyped URL gets Netlify's generic branded page rather than the site's.
  - No robots.txt and no sitemap. 23 pages with nothing telling a crawler they exist.
  - Favicon is still the default Astro logo (the purple rocket) at public/favicon.svg and public/favicon.ico.
  - No og:image, so sharing any link produces a bare text card. The Drift photo or a Resonant Landscapes still would both work.

@astrojs/sitemap handles the sitemap and robots in one step. The 404 is a src/pages/404.astro using the existing Base layout.
design: astro.config.mjs, src/pages/404.astro, public/, src/layouts/Base.astro for the og:image meta.
acceptance_criteria: A wrong URL renders the site's own 404. robots.txt and sitemap are served. Favicon is not Astro's. Sharing a link shows an image.
close_reason: 404.astro using the Base layout; robots.txt pointing at the sitemap; @astrojs/sitemap with site set to https://www.tatecarson.com (23 URLs, 404 excluded, no invented changefreq/priority); favicon replaced with a slab-serif T monogram in the site's ink and cream, with PNG and apple-touch fallbacks generated by scripts/make-icons.mjs; og:image at 1200x630 cropped from the Palisades photo, with work pages overriding it with their own thumbnail. Also added canonical, og:url, og:site_name and twitter:card.

title: Heading structure is invalid for screen readers and search
description:
Visually invisible, because .prose h1/h2 are styled as small mono labels, but the document outline is wrong.

Home page:
  - No h1 for the page itself. 'Tate Carson' is only a link in the rail.
  - Four h1 elements, all from migrated markdown subsections: 'Assistant Professor of Digital Sound Design', 'Journal Articles', 'Conference Papers', 'Dissertation'.

Work pages:
  - Two h1 elements — the work title from the template, plus a heading from the body markdown. Two archived bodies use '#' for subsections (swarm.md, sounds-aware.md).
  - sounds-aware repeats its own title as a body heading, 'Sounds Aware Project Overview'.

A screen reader announces four top-level headings and no page title.

Fix by demoting '#' to '##' in migrated bodies (a transform in scripts/migrate.mjs, so it survives a re-run) and giving each page a single real h1.
design: scripts/migrate.mjs for the body transform; src/pages/index.astro and src/pages/works/[...slug].astro for the page h1.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one h1 per page, and it names the page. Heading levels descend without skipping.
close_reason: Home page has one h1 (the rail name, now a real heading with the section links moved into their own nav rather than the whole rail being one). Migrated page bodies are demoted by a per-page offset in scripts/migrate.mjs so each starts below the section heading above it. Work bodies: swarm's stray '#' demoted, sounds-aware's title-repeating '#' wrapper dropped, and-the-water-receded's orphan '###' promoted to h2. Prose CSS extended to h4/h5 on the index and h3 on work pages, which was previously unstyled. Verified across all 24 built pages: exactly one h1 each, zero level skips.

title: About prose reads as promotional boilerplate
description:
The About text carried over from the old site is the weakest writing on the page, and it is the second thing a visitor reads. Phrases present:

  - 'cutting-edge curricula'
  - 'rapidly evolving field of digital sound design'
  - 'His commitment to mentorship and curriculum development continues to prepare students for careers in...'
  - 'garnered international attention'
  - 'emphasizes hands-on learning and interdisciplinary collaboration'

This is faculty-profile press-release register. It reads as generated whether or not it was, and it clashes with the work blurbs, which are concrete and specific ('BART trains and a Chinese New Year parade — the industrial and the ceremonial — collide across eight speakers'). The blurbs sound like a composer; the bio sounds like an HR page.

This is Tate's own professional self-description, so the rewrite is his call rather than something to change unilaterally. Decision needed before any edit.
design: src/content/pages/about.md, generated from the archive by scripts/migrate.mjs.
acceptance_criteria: Either the bio is rewritten in the register the work blurbs use, or the current text is explicitly kept and this issue is closed as won't-fix.
notes:
Shares its premise with tc-c8k (work page bodies have no shared shape or
register). Both argue from the same observation — the work blurbs are the
strongest, most consistent writing on the site, and everything else should be
read against them — and both are Tate's own words, so both are his call rather
than something to change unilaterally.

Different files (src/content/pages/about.md here, src/content/works/*.md there)
and neither acceptance criterion touches the other, so they are not blocking.
But settling a register for one and not the other leaves the About page and the
work pages sounding different from each other, which is the same defect one
level up. Whoever decides either should decide both.

title: The intro paragraph is duplicated verbatim in About
description:
The paragraph at the top of the ledger is word-for-word the first two sentences of the About section (02):

  'Tate Carson, PhD, is an Assistant Professor of Digital Sound Design at Dakota State University (DSU), where he has been teaching since 2021. His research and creative practice center on participatory mobile music, web audio, and locative media.'

A visitor reads the same sentences twice within one scroll, and the second time is the moment they clicked 'About' expecting something new.

Fix either by trimming the opening of about.md, or by replacing the intro with something that does a different job — a one-line positioning statement rather than a biography opening.

Note that about.md is generated by scripts/migrate.mjs from the archive, so an edit to the markdown alone will be overwritten on the next run. It needs a transform in that script, in the manner of DEAD_LINKS or DROP_LINES.
acceptance_criteria: The opening sentences appear once on the page.

title: The rail's CV link renders faded despite opacity: 1
description:
src/pages/index.astro sets opacity: 0.6 on .rail__connect and then opacity: 1 on
.rail__cv to lift the CV download back out of it. That does not work: opacity on
an ancestor composites the whole subtree, so a descendant can never render more
opaque than its parent. The CV link is drawn at 0.6 like every other link in the
list.

The comment above the rule states the intent plainly — 'the one link in the rail
people actively look for, so it carries the accent rather than sitting at the
list's 0.6 opacity' — so the design decision is already made and simply is not
taking effect. It still reads as accent-coloured, just muted.

Verified in the browser: .rail__connect computes to 0.6, .rail__cv computes to 1,
and the effective rendered opacity is the product.

The same bug was introduced and then fixed in src/pages/404.astro in the ledger/
headings/SEO branch — move the fade onto the links themselves rather than the
list, and note that .rail__connect a outweighs .rail__cv on specificity, so the
override needs to be .rail__connect a.rail__cv or equivalent.
design: src/pages/index.astro — .rail__connect and .rail__cv. See the .links / .links a.links__home pair in src/pages/404.astro for the shape of the fix.
acceptance_criteria: The CV link in the rail renders at full strength while the other connect links stay at 0.6. Confirmed by computed style, not by eye.
close_reason: The fade moved from .rail__connect onto .rail__connect a, so the CV rule is no longer trying to climb out of a parent compositing group. The override also needed matching on .rail__connect a.rail__cv — a bare .rail__cv loses to .rail__connect a on specificity, which is what went wrong on the first attempt at the same fix in 404.astro. Verified: list opacity 1, CV link 1 in the accent, Email/Github/Scholar 0.6.

title: README describes a site structure that no longer exists
description:
Two passages drifted:

  - The opening says the home page is 'works ... followed by about, publications,
    teaching, and CV'. The CV section was removed in eff3432; the download lives
    in the rail now.

  - The field table says tag is 'One of six: Fixed media, Web / app,
    Installation, Score, Performance, Film'. The actual enum in
    src/content.config.ts has eight and shares only one name with that list:
    Smartphone, Fixed Media, Live Electroacoustic Music, Live Electronics,
    Improvising Acoustic Ensemble, Dance, Film, Sound Sculpture.

The second is the one that matters — someone adding a work would pick a tag from
the README and fail the build.
design: README.md. The tag list should point at src/content.config.ts rather than restate it, so it cannot drift again.
acceptance_criteria: README matches the code. The tag list is not duplicated anywhere it can go stale.
close_reason: Opening paragraph now describes about/research/teaching and states that there is no CV section because the page is itself a CV. The tag row points at the TAGS enum in src/content.config.ts rather than restating it, so it cannot drift again. Also added the two rows the table was missing entirely, research and the new repo.

title: Two work bodies link to the old site's absolute URLs
description:
Two migrated bodies point at the archived site rather than at this one:

  src/content/works/sounds-aware.md
    https://www.tatecarson.com/papers/SoundsAware_CameraReady.pdf
